en-GB: For surface area, we'll assume the standard right square pyramid: its apex is directly above the centre of the base.
Given... s equals six centimetres. And h equals four centimetres.
Here is the pyramid, with base side s equals six centimetres and perpendicular height h equals four centimetres.
s is the side length of the square base, and h is the perpendicular height from the base to the apex. We want V, the volume, and TSA, the total surface area.
Look at the pyramid on the board. Its base is a square, and the apex sits directly above the centre of that square.
The label s equals six centimetres is the side length of that square base.
The label h equals four centimetres is the perpendicular height, the straight vertical distance from the base up to the apex.
Start with volume. For any pyramid, V equals one third times the base area times the perpendicular height.
The base is a square, so its area is s squared. That gives V equals one third s squared h.
Substitute the given values. V equals one third times six squared times four.
Six squared is thirty-six, and thirty-six times four is one hundred and forty-four. So V equals one hundred and forty-four over three.
That division gives forty-eight. So the volume equals forty-eight cubic centimetres.

Now for surface area we need the slant height l, the height of each triangular face. The apex sits directly above the centre of the base, so the slant height is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with legs h and half of s.
Half of s is three. Substitute: l equals the square root of four squared plus three squared.
Four squared is sixteen and three squared is nine, so l equals the square root of twenty-five.
The square root of twenty-five is five. So the slant height equals five centimetres.
Total surface area is the base area plus the four triangular faces. Each triangle has area one half times s times l, so TSA equals s squared plus two s l.
Substitute the values. TSA equals six squared plus two times six times five.
Six squared is thirty-six, and two times six times five is sixty. So TSA equals thirty-six plus sixty.
Under that assumption, the total surface area equals ninety-six square centimetres.
Check the slant height: a three, four, five right-angled triangle, which is consistent. And the volume, one third of thirty-six times four, equals forty-eight, so both results agree.
